add.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract add export <name> [--dry-run] | add check <Name> [--dry-run]

`add export` edits package.json exports, the bundler entry, the declaration shim, the documentation entry points, the
dead-code entry and docs/surface.json, and creates the module, its test and a draft changeset.
`add check AmbientCapabilities` names the check in package.json, with its settings written out to change.

Options:
  --dry-run                print what would be written and change nothing

doctor.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract doctor

Read-only. Lists what is in place, the command that fixes each thing that is missing, and the steps that
cannot be scripted (npm's trusted publisher, repository settings, review apps) with the exact values to enter.
Exits 1 while anything is left to run.

env.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract env [--check | --rotation-issue]

Writes docs/ENVIRONMENT.md from ci/env.schema.ts, with env-cap, which this package carries.
Nothing is required: no schema means nothing to document, and a missing owner or expiry date is a warning.

Options:
  --check                  write nothing; fail and name what is stale
  --rotation-issue         open, update or close the GitHub issue for credentials due for rotation

exceptions.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract exceptions

Read-only inventory of the records in .repo-contract/exceptions.

generate.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract generate [--check]

Rewrites only what is between the <!-- ipc:begin ... --> and <!-- ipc:end ... --> markers of the documents it
reads, formatted with the package's own Prettier settings.

Options:
  --check                  write nothing; fail and name what is stale

init.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract init [--name <package>] [options]

In an existing package: adds the pin and the scripts and tools the checks need, installs, writes every config,
workflow, document and template the package lacks (never overwriting one it has), drafts docs/surface.json,
starts adoption mode and generates the API map. With --name, in an empty directory: scaffolds a complete new
package. It refuses to start over uncommitted changes and ends with `doctor`. Running it again finishes what is
missing.

Options:
  --name <package>         start a new package in this empty directory
  --owner <owner>          the GitHub owner of the repository (default: its remote)
  --description <text>     the new package's description
  --tag vX.Y.Z             the release to pin (default: the latest)
  --spec <spec>            pin exactly this dependency spec, for a fork or a local copy
  --strict                 skip adoption mode: every check can fail the run from the start
  --github                 also apply branch protection through the gh CLI
  --docs                   replace a shared document the package has with the standard's
  --force                  overwrite scaffolded files that already exist
  --dry-run                print the plan and change nothing

install-hooks.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract install-hooks

Sets core.hooksPath to the standard's hooks. Never run by an install script.

mutation.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract mutation [--base <ref>] [file...]

Runs every mutant of the files the change touched, and of the source files the changed tests import, and nothing
else; always every mutant of those files, never an earlier result, under the package's own concurrency. It is advice,
not the gate: a mutant in a file nobody touched can be killed by a test that did, so only a full `Mutation` run says a
change is finished.

Options:
  --base <ref>             what the change is measured against (default: origin/main, else main)
  file...                  mutate exactly these files instead

new.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract new adr "<title>"

Writes the next numbered record in specs/decisions (or docs/decisions, docs/adr) with each section's prompt.
The prompts fail a release until they are answered.

promote.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract promote <Check>... | --all

While a package is adopting the standard a failing check is reported but does not fail the run. Promoting a
check makes its failure fail the run from then on. --all ends adoption mode.

report.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract report [--base <ref>] [--out <file>]

Reads git, the pending changesets, the exception registries, the decision records, the manifest and the contract's
last report, and says what changed, what it means for a release, and what the checks said. Nothing is written by hand.
Run the contract first so the report can say what the checks found.

Options:
  --base <ref>             what to measure against (default: origin/main, else main)
  --out <file>             write the report to a file instead of printing it

site.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract site [--check] [--content <file>] [--out <dir>]

Writes index.html, brief.html, styles.css and script.js from docs/site.json.

Options:
  --check                  write nothing; fail and name what is stale

skill.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract skill [--check]

Writes skills/<name>/SKILL.md and skills/<name>/references/api.md from docs/skill.json (what only the author knows:
when it applies, one example, the rules, the mistakes that matter) and what the package already holds (its entry points,
its public API, its version). The manual has a word budget, so an agent can load it whole; everything longer is a link.
Prints the address to give an agent.

Options:
  --check                  write nothing; fail and name what is stale, over budget or broken

sync.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract sync [--apply [--update]] [--add <copy>]

Compares the files the standard owns here (workflows, the Changesets config, shared code and documents) with
the standard's, and shows what differs.

Options:
  --apply                  write the files that are missing
  --update                 with --apply, also replace the files that drifted
  --add <copy>             start carrying a managed copy of shared code or a shared document

sync-benchmark-guides.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract sync-benchmark-guides

Writes the shared guides that explain how to write and how to read the benchmarks.

tool.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract tool <name> [args]

The helpers every package used to copy: `size` checks the gzip budgets in ci/size-budgets.mjs, `badges` writes the coverage and size badges,
`api-report` fails when docs/api-report/ is out of date, `cjs-interop` makes require() of the ESLint plugin return the plugin,
`compiler-isolation` fails when a client entry can reach the bundled compiler, and `ambient` gives the
AmbientCapabilities answer without running the contract. Run one from the package's root.

Options:
  size --json <file>       also write the measured sizes, which `badges` reads

update-baseline.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract update-baseline

Rewrites the committed baselines the ApiContract and SurfaceContract checks compare against.

upgrade.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract upgrade <vX.Y.Z>

Installs the release, re-pins the workflows that call its reusable workflows and brings the managed files up to
date. Then it regenerates the generated regions and, where the package has them, the agent skill,
docs/ENVIRONMENT.md and the landing page, and copies the benchmark guides. The API and surface baselines are
left to the package's own release. It stops at the first step that fails.

verify-consumers.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract verify-consumers <checkout>... [--skip a,b] [--keep]

For each checkout, runs its contract's fast offline checks twice in throwaway copies, once with the standard it has
installed and once with this one, and reports every check that got worse. A check that fails both ways was already failing
and is not blamed on the change. The checkout itself is never touched.

Options:
  --skip a,b               also leave these checks out
  --keep                   keep the throwaway copies, to look at what ran

internal-package-contract.help:
Usage: internal-package-contract [command] [options]

Reusable CI checks, workflows and document generators shared by every MaverickCER package, added and kept current with one command.
Together they are the standard: `init` adds it, `upgrade` keeps it current. With no command, runs every check.

Start:
  init                       bring this package under the standard, or start a new one with --name <package>
  doctor                     what is set up, what to run next, and the steps only a person can take

Daily:
  (none)                     run the whole contract
  generate                   write the generated regions of the documents from package.json and docs/surface.json
  skill                      write the package's agent skill: a short manual an AI loads, and a reference of every public signature
  mutation                   mutation-test what a change touched, as a fast loop (the full run is the check)
  report                     what this change does to the package, as Markdown to paste into a pull request
  env                        document the variables and secrets the package needs, from ci/env.schema.ts
  tool                       run a build or release helper: size, badges, api-report, cjs-interop, compiler-isolation, ambient
  add                        wire a new subpath export into every place that lists one, or turn on an optional check
  new                        start a decision record with the next number, its sections and prompts
  promote                    make a check fail the run; --all ends adoption mode

Maintain:
  verify-consumers           check that this version of the standard does not make a package that depends on it worse
  upgrade                    move to a release and bring everything it owns up to date
  sync                       report the files the standard owns here that are missing or drifted
  site                       generate the landing page and one-page brief from docs/site.json
  exceptions                 list every exception registry: counts by type, legacy, expired
  update-baseline            regenerate the API and surface baselines after a release
  sync-benchmark-guides      copy the canonical benchmark guides into benchmarks/
  install-hooks              point git at the bundled hooks (once per clone)

Run `internal-package-contract <command> --help` for a command's options.

Options (when running the contract):
  --checks a,b               run only checks a and b (and what they depend on)
  --skip a,b                 run every check except a and b
  --changed                  run only the checks the changed files can affect
  --scope <mode>             full, affected or auto: narrow tests, mutation and CRAP to what the change can reach (default: full)
  --base <ref>               the ref an affected or auto scope compares against
  --json                     print the report as JSON on stdout and nothing else
  --logs <mode>              write a log per check: all, failing or off (default: failing)
  --strict                   also fail on a "not evaluated" result no exception covers (the default under CI)
  --no-strict                turn --strict off under CI
  -h, --help                 print this text and exit
